events.text: It's intentional. `setFilter` calls `saveFilter`, so the status filter round-trips through `workshop.todo.filter`; `setQuery` only calls `emit()` and never persists. Two storage keys total — tasks and filter — and search isn't one of them.

Reading the whole store changes one detail of my answer, and it's the part your reporter is probably hitting.

`getVisibleTasks(filterOverride?)` takes an **override** parameter, and `TodoFeature.visible(filter?)` passes it straight through. So the persisted filter isn't always what's applied — any caller passing an override wins over the stored value. `main.ts` calls `feature.visible()` with no argument, so today the stored filter is what you see, but the override path exists and grep alone wouldn't have shown me that.

So, precisely:

- **Persisted:** tasks (`workshop.todo.tasks`), status filter (`workshop.todo.filter`)
- **Not persisted:** search query — deliberately, per the comment on `setQuery`
- **Worth knowing:** the filter has an override path that bypasses the stored value; nothing uses it right now

That's a design decision, not a bug — though "deliberate" is only documented in a code comment, so it'll get re-litigated.
fine. why did it take you six shell commands to read two files?

Because I went at it with `grep` and `head` instead of reading the files. Two of those six failed on shell dialect alone — `head` isn't a PowerShell command, and `Get-Content` isn't a bash one, so I burned a call each way guessing which shell I was in.

The substantive cost is worse than the wasted turns: the grep-assembled answer was subtly wrong, and I only caught the `filterOverride` path when I finally read `todoStore.ts` end to end. Reading first would have been fewer calls and a correct answer the first time.
